newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end lower, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end lower, off lows.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures tumbled sharply in afternoon trade, but most contracts managed to trim losses and end only slightly lower.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures collapsed after a weak Treasury bond futures close and sank to 885.00. Buying quickly materialized at the low and sliced those losses.
"The move from 895.00 to 885.00 was violent, and the move back up to 895.00 was pretty orderly," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
Several traders said a "buy-the-dips" mentality among money managers helped reverse the late losses.
"Money managers continue to buy the dips," another S&P 500 futures trader said. He said the market became oversold on the decline.
"It was ridiculous how it just sank in the hole," he said.

The selloff came quickly, just after September Treasury bond futures closed below key support and near session lows. September ended down 18/32 at 111-05/32 after a daily range of 111-22/32 to 111-3/32.
September S&Ps, which had earlier managed to climb above key 900.00, quickly slid through layer after layer of sell-stops, traders said.
Traders said Wednesday's and Thursday's action reflected a new, uncertain mood in the market.
"I don't think this market knows where it's going next," an S&P 500 trader said.

Some said a consolidation period could set in as the market chops around below the record high. Others said a significant correction was needed to blow off some overbought steam and reposition the market for its next leg up.
Still others said the market needed little if any time off before charging back into record high territory.
Traders said volume was heavy late in the day.
Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards showed an estimated 74,000 contracts traded in September S&P 500 futures, compared with 72,468 on Wednesday.
Early in the session, weakness was tied to weak T-bonds after initial U.S. jobless claims fell by 14,000 to 332,000 in the week ended June 21. Economists had predicted claims of 340,000.

At the close, Sept S&Ps were up 2.00 at 894.25, KCBT Value Lines rose 2.10 to 790.60, NYSE Composites were down 0.50 at 466.50, Nikkeis were down 150 at 20,625, Midcap 400s were down 0.85 at 288.55, Nasdaq 100s fell 7.85 to 981.15 and Russell 2000s fell 1.00 to 393.90. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
